      "representation": "I. Şuvaina studies generalized rational blowdowns of complex surfaces containing linear chains corresponding to cyclic quotient singularities of type 1/n²(1,nm−1). If the contracted orbifold surface has ample canonical sheaf, it carries a negative orbifold Kähler–Einstein metric. For the resulting symplectic manifold N, Seiberg–Witten theory gives ∫_N s_g²dμ_g≥32π²c₁²(N) for every metric. Şuvaina constructs metrics by deleting small neighborhoods of orbifold points and gluing in rescaled ALE rational homology balls or ADE spaces. On the interpolation annuli, g_t differs from the Euclidean metric by O(t²), its first derivatives are O(t), and second derivatives are uniformly bounded; hence scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded while the annular volume tends to zero.       "title": "Desingularizations of Conformally Kaehler, Einstein Orbifolds",
      "representation": "Claude LeBrun and Tristan Ozuch study sequences of smooth compact oriented positive-Einstein four-manifolds converging to a compact Einstein orbifold whose metric is Hermitian or conformally Kähler. They define admissible sequences by requiring every Ricci-flat ALE bubble to be anti-self-dual. Such bubbles are classified through type-T singularities, including SU(2) and specified cyclic U(2) groups. The paper reviews the compactness and bubbling picture, reconstructs smooth manifolds by replacing orbifold points with ALE spaces, and proves that admissible limits of Hermitian Einstein orbifolds have Del Pezzo underlying topology and satisfy c1^2(X)=(2χ+3τ)(M). It obtains the group-order estimate |Γk|<12/(2χ+3τ)(M). The analytic construction uses gauged Einstein operators, Lichnerowicz linearization, weighted Hölder spaces, obstruction extensions, naïve desingularizations, higher-order approximate Einstein-modulo-obstruction metrics, and iterative partial desingularizations. For a single bubble, multiple bubbles, and bubble trees, the authors prove residual estimates such as o(t), o(tk), and o(Tk+1), together with closeness estimates for the corrected metrics. They establish that the eigenvalues of the self-dual Weyl curvature of approximate and corrected metrics remain uniformly close to those of the orbifold limit, including uniformly across bubble-tree regions. Since a conformally Kähler positive-Einstein metric has the relevant Weyl eigenvalue pattern, the desingularized metrics satisfy det(W+)>0; LeBrun–Wu rigidity then implies that sufficiently late smooth Einstein metrics are conformally Kähler, and ultimately Kähler-Einstein except for two rigid exceptional manifolds. The cited bibliography includes Anderson (1989), Bando (1990), Bando–Kasue–Nakajima (1989), Kronheimer (1989), Şuvaina (2012), Wright (2012), Biquard (2013, 2016), and Ozuch (2021, 2022).",

      "title": "Moduli spaces of critical Riemannian metrics in dimension ...",
      "representation": "Gang Tian and Jeff Viaclovsky, “Moduli Spaces of Critical Riemannian Metrics in Dimension Four,” dated December 16, 2003. The paper studies compactness in dimension four for three classes: half-conformally flat metrics with constant scalar curvature, metrics with harmonic curvature, and Kähler metrics with constant scalar curvature. It defines a critical metric to mean one of these classes and records the relevant elliptic curvature equations, including ΔRic = Rm * Ric; the Euler–Lagrange equation of the Weyl functional is the Bach-flat equation. The main compactness theorem considers critical metrics on smooth complete pointed four-manifolds with uniformly bounded Sobolev constants, uniformly bounded total ∫|Rm|², a positive volume lower bound, and uniformly bounded first Betti numbers. A subsequence converges to a connected critical Riemannian multi-fold with finite singular set, without splitting off a compact orbifold; noncompact limits are ALE of order τ for every τ<2, and if b1=0 the limit is an orbifold. A closed unit-volume version replaces the volume lower bound by Vol=1. A local-Sobolev version is also stated for compact manifolds. The paper provides epsilon-regularity under small local L2 curvature and Sobolev control, volume growth estimates, removable singularity results, bubbling analysis, and stronger Kähler/orbifold conclusions. It explicitly remarks that the general Bach-flat case has weaker regularity conclusions and that removing the Sobolev assumption and treating collapsing are open problems. The paper does not claim compactness for arbitrary metrics or arbitrary almost-minimizing sequences, and its criticality notions are not equivalent to the Einstein equation.",

      "representation": "R. Răsdeac̦onu and I. Şuvaina study ALE Ricci-flat Kähler surfaces and their compactifications. The relevant quotient singularities are exactly class T: rational double points, corresponding to finite SU(2) subgroups and Gorenstein/hyperkähler smoothings, or cyclic singularities 1/(dn^2)(1,dnm−1), with d>0, n≥1, gcd(m,n)=1, corresponding to non-hyperkähler Q-Gorenstein smoothings and torsion canonical bundles on the smooth fibers. The paper gives the explicit cyclic model (xy=P(z^n))/μ_n inside C^3/(1/n)(1,−1,m), derives the universal Q-Gorenstein deformation, and states that a generic smooth fiber is the Milnor fiber; nonsmooth fibers have at worst A-type rational double points, whose minimal resolution is diffeomorphic to the Milnor fiber. It constructs compactifications in weighted projective spaces. For cyclic class-T fibers, the compactifying divisor C is rational and ample, with formulas −K̄=((c+n)/n)C in one construction and −K̃=((k+c)/k)C in another; the compactification is a log del Pezzo orbifold, while resolving rational-double-point singularities gives K_N=p^*K_M and generally only an almost-ample boundary.       "representation": "A research paper by Hans-Joachim Hein, Song Sun, Jeff Viaclovsky, and Ruobing Zhang constructs families of collapsing Ricci-flat Kähler (hyperkähler) metrics on K3 surfaces. The metrics collapse to an interval; regular fibers are 3-tori or 3-dimensional Heisenberg nilmanifolds, while Tian–Yau and Taub–NUT spaces arise as bubbles. The construction uses the Gibbons–Hawking ansatz, gluing, weighted Schauder estimates, Liouville theorems, and perturbation to genuine hyperkähler metrics. If the rank is exactly n−k, curvature is uniformly bounded on B_1(p); conversely, the stated curvature bound implies maximal rank. The paper defines nilpotent rank using the lower central series. It remarks that replacing the Einstein assumption by bounded Ricci curvature yields bounded C^{1,α}-covering geometry, not a curvature bound. In the four-dimensional codimension-one regions of the construction, regular nilmanifold fibers give rank 3 and hence uniform curvature estimates, whereas singular fibers have lower rank and curvature blow-up.
